# Lisbon Family Trip Snapshot: 2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13

A relaxed 4-day plan for 2 adults and 2 kids, centered on museums, viewpoints, and one beach day. I’ve kept it to **no more than 2 major activities per day** and targeted the full trip at **about €1,430–€1,580** excluding flights.

# Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary and Budget

## Day 1: Historic Center + River Views
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: **Baixa + Praça do Comércio** stroll, then ride the **Santa Justa area** for city-center views.
- Afternoon: **Lisbon Story Centre** or a lighter museum stop, followed by a slow walk along the riverfront.
- Transit tip: Use the **Metro + walking**; this is the easiest low-stress first day.
- Rainy-day backup: Swap the outdoor walk for **Museu de Lisboa** or the **Lisbon Story Centre** and add a long lunch nearby.
- Estimated cost: **€95–€150** for transport, museum tickets, snacks, and lunch.

## Day 2: Alfama + Castelo Viewpoints
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Explore **Alfama** with a short scenic climb to a viewpoint such as **Miradouro de Santa Luzia**.
- Afternoon: Visit **Castelo de São Jorge** for the best family-friendly historic viewpoint day.
- Transit tip: Use **tram/ride-hail for the uphill part**, then walk downhill through Alfama.
- Rainy-day backup: Replace the viewpoint walk with **Museu do Fado** plus a longer Alfama lunch stop.
- Estimated cost: **€110–€170** for entry fees, tram/ride-hail, and meals.

## Day 3: Beach Day at Cascais
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Head to **Cascais** for an easy beach morning and promenade time.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3c/Beach_near_Lisbon_Portugal%2C_1994..jpg Alt=Morning: Head to **Cascais** for an easy beach morning and promenade time, Lisbon, Portugal
- Afternoon: Keep it light with the **old town + marina** or a short seaside snack break before returning.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4c/Lisbon_%281600%29_detail_1.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Keep it light with the **old town + marina** or a short seaside snack break before returning, Lisbon, Portugal
- Transit tip: Take the **train from Cais do Sodré to Cascais**; it is simple, scenic, and kid-friendly.
- Rainy-day backup: If the weather turns, switch to **Oceanário de Lisboa** instead of the beach.
- Estimated cost: **€140–€220** for train fares, beach snacks, lunch, and optional rentals.
Media: Alt=Estimated cost: **€140–€220** for train fares, beach snacks, lunch, and optional rentals, Lisbon, Portugal

## Day 4: Belém Museums + Waterfront
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Visit **Belém** for one major museum or monument, ideally **Jerónimos Monastery** or **MAAT** depending on your family’s interest.
- Afternoon: Enjoy the **riverfront** and a relaxed stop for **pastéis de nata** before wrapping up.
- Transit tip: Use **tram, bus, or ride-hail**; Belém is easier when you avoid overpacking the day.
- Rainy-day backup: Choose **MAAT** if you want a strong indoor option, or **Coach Museum** for a more classic family museum day.
- Estimated cost: **€120–€190** for tickets, transit, and food.

# Budget Fit for 2 Adults + 2 Kids

## Estimated Trip Cost Breakdown
| Category | Estimated Cost |
|---|---:|
| Lodging, 4 nights | €560–€760 |
| Food and drinks | €360–€480 |
| Local transit | €70–€110 |
| Tickets and activities | €320–€420 |
| Beach extras / snacks / buffer | €80–€120 |
| Total | **€1,390–€1,890** |

Best-fit target: with a mid-range apartment and a couple of paid museum entries, you should land around **€1,500–€1,580**.
To stay safely under **€1,600**, keep:
- lodging near a metro stop
- lunch simple on 2 of the 4 days
- only 1–2 paid museum/monument entries per day

# Transit Tips for a Relaxed Family Pace

- **Best base areas:** Baixa, Chiado, Avenida, or near Cais do Sodré for easier train access to Cascais.
- **Best family transit mix:** Metro + walking + occasional tram/ride-hail for hills.
- **Avoid over-scheduling hills:** Alfama and Castelo are beautiful but tiring; use transport to reach the top, then walk down.
- **For kids:** Build in a snack break every 2–3 hours to keep the pace easy.
